title: Ethiopian Chicken Firfir
community: All of Ethiopia — the Doro Wat sauce firfir
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Doro Firfir — torn day-old injera tossed with Doro Wat sauce and shredded chicken, kibbeh, and berbere. The most celebrated firfir — made with yesterday's Doro Wat, it transforms the greatest Ethiopian dish into a brilliant next-day breakfast.
longDesc: Doro Firfir is the morning after Doro Wat — the leftover berbere sauce and shredded chicken tossed with torn day-old injera and additional kibbeh produces a firfir of extraordinary depth. Ethiopian families look forward to Doro Firfir almost as much as Doro Wat itself.
ingredients: 3 pieces day-old injera (ETH001) — torn into pieces
1 cup Doro Wat sauce (ETH061) — warmed, with shredded chicken
steps: Heat kibbeh in a wide pan.
Add warmed Doro Wat sauce with its chicken.
Add torn injera. Toss to coat every piece.
Cook 3—4 minutes, tossing, until injera has absorbed the sauce.
chefTips: Day-old injera absorbs better than fresh.
The Doro Wat sauce must be warmed — cold sauce does not penetrate the injera.
Serve the instant it is done — Doro Firfir becomes heavy if it sits.
commonMistakes: Fresh injera — absorbs too fast, becomes mushy.
cookingScience: See ETH032 for firfir cooking science. Doro Firfir has a particularly complex flavour because the Doro Wat sauce already contains 25—30 minutes of Maillard-reaction onion compounds, berbere carotenoids, and chicken gelatin — all of which are reheated and further concentrated when tossed with the injera.
sustainabilityTips: The ultimate celebration leftover dish — zero waste from Doro Wat.
healthBenefits: All the nutrition of Doro Wat in a new form.
culturalNote: Doro Firfir is proof that Ethiopian cooking produces no waste and creates no lesser dish by recycling — the morning-after firfir made from Doro Wat is celebrated in its own right, anticipated by the family almost as eagerly as the original feast.
